extracted.intended_audience: prospective grant applicants and organizational grantees seeking Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation funding (global health-focused nonprofits, research institutions, program teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and processes the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation uses to select, evaluate, and monitor grant-funded initiatives, with special notes for the Grand Challenges program. Intended to guide proposal preparation, evaluation, and post-award reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address significant health challenges faced by vulnerable populations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should address significant health challenges faced by vulnerable populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is given to initiatives that target major health needs among the most vulnerable groups; proposals should clearly identify the vulnerable population being served and the health challenge's significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target diseases with high morbidity and mortality rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation prioritizes work that targets diseases with high morbidity and mortality rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should justify the burden of disease (morbidity/mortality) and show how their work addresses diseases with substantial health impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on diseases affecting children and women in low-income countries
rubrics_metrics.description: Particular focus on diseases affecting children and women in low-income countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals addressing maternal, newborn, child health and issues disproportionately affecting women in low-income settings are especially prioritized; include demographic and contextual data to support this focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate innovation and scalability
rubrics_metrics.description: Initiatives should demonstrate innovation and the potential to scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must describe what is novel about the approach (scientific or programmatic) and provide a plausible pathway and evidence for how the intervention or solution could be scaled to reach larger populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial screening for strategic alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals undergo screening to ensure alignment with the foundation's strategic priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before detailed review, proposals are checked for fit with stated strategy and program goals; proposals misaligned with strategy may be filtered out at this stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific validity of the proposed work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert reviewers evaluate whether the scientific rationale, hypotheses, and underlying evidence are sound and credible; include literature support and a clear conceptual framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of feasibility of the proposed approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider whether proposed methods, timelines, staffing, and resources make the project achievable; address operational risks and mitigation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the potential for the project to achieve meaningful impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the expected health outcomes and population-level effects; include plausible effect sizes, pathways to impact, and how success will change current practice or conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evidence-based metrics to measure potential outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation uses evidence-based metrics to measure potential outcomes and emphasizes data in decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should ground expected outcomes in evidence and explain metric selection; emphasize rigorous, measurable indicators tied to outcomes rather than outputs alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust plans for monitoring and evaluation (M&E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include robust plans for monitoring and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an M&E framework that specifies what will be measured, when, and by whom; include methods, data sources, analysis plans, and how learning will inform adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must state clear objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives should be specific, measurable, and linked to indicators and outcomes in the M&E plan; avoid vague or overly broad objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key performance indicators (KPIs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must identify key performance indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define KPIs that track progress toward objectives, include baseline and target values where possible, and justify why chosen indicators appropriately reflect progress and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outlined methods for data collection and analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must outline methods for data collection and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe instruments, frequency, sampling, data quality controls, analytical approaches, and ethical/data-protection considerations; show capacity to implement the proposed data plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative definition of overall results and data during award setup
rubrics_metrics.description: From the earliest phases, the foundation works with grantees to define overall results, data needed, and how to evaluate that data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-award, grantees should expect to collaborate on setting results frameworks and data needs; be prepared to refine indicators and measurement approaches with foundation staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent evaluators for objective assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation employs independent evaluators to conduct assessments of funded projects at various stages to provide objective analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees should anticipate independent evaluations at midline, endline, or other stages; design projects and data systems to support external evaluation and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct relevance to Grand Challenges goals
rubrics_metrics.description: For Grand Challenges, ideas must have direct relevance to the defined Grand Challenges goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals to Grand Challenges must explicitly map how the idea addresses the specific problem statement or goals of that Grand Challenges call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel scientific approach for Grand Challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Grand Challenges seeks high innovation and a novel scientific approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase I proposals should emphasize novelty and how the approach departs from or advances beyond existing solutions; explain the scientific rationale for novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable milestones within short Phase I timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Grand Challenges Phase I requires measurable milestones within short timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define concrete, short-term milestones that can be assessed within Phase I; these milestones should demonstrate feasibility and inform decisions about follow-on funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advancement potential for follow-on Phase II funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Grand Challenges proposals should show potential to advance to follow-on Phase II funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate the criteria and evidence that would justify scaling or advancing to Phase II, including what Phase I will achieve to make that case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding exclusions: no tuition or K-12 education
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation does not fund tuition or K-12 education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants proposing tuition support or K-12 educational programs should not expect funding; ensure the proposed activities fall within eligible program types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding exclusions: no direct unrestricted individual funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation does not provide direct unrestricted funding for individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals seeking personal unrestricted support are not eligible; applicants should be organizations and propose charitable or educational uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant designation requirement (charitable/educational purposes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants are designated for charitable and/or educational purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must describe how funds will be used for charitable or educational objectives and comply with grant terms restricting use to those purposes.
